reference.source: Sleisenger and Fordtran's Gastrointestinal and Liver Disease
clinicalPearls: Refers to calcification of the gallbladder wall, generally the end result of long-standing chronic cholecystitis and almost always associated with gallstones
Frequently asymptomatic and discovered incidentally on plain radiography, CT, or ultrasound
Historically linked to a high risk of gallbladder carcinoma, though contemporary series suggest the risk, while real, is lower than once believed
The pattern of calcification may matter, with selective mucosal or incomplete calcification thought to carry more risk than diffuse transmural (complete) calcification
CT is the most reliable modality for demonstrating and characterising the mural calcification
Prophylactic cholecystectomy is commonly recommended given the malignancy association, particularly for surgically fit patients or when features are concerning
Coexisting focal wall thickening or a mass should raise suspicion of established carcinoma
reference.pathophysiology: Porcelain gallbladder develops from chronic inflammation of the gallbladder, almost invariably in the setting of gallstones and often after repeated or persistent cholecystitis. Prolonged mucosal injury and scarring lead to deposition of calcium salts within the fibrotic gallbladder wall, which may be laid down as a continuous intramural band (complete calcification) or as patchy calcification of the mucosa and inner layers (selective or incomplete calcification). The stiff, calcified wall is functionally useless and characteristically painless. The chronic inflammatory milieu that produces the calcification is also the substrate for malignant transformation, which accounts for the recognised association with gallbladder adenocarcinoma.
additionalDifferentials: Emphysematous cholecystitis (gas rather than calcium in the wall)
additionalInvestigations: CT to confirm and characterise the extent and pattern of wall calcification
Abdominal ultrasound to assess the wall, gallstones, and any mass
MRI when soft-tissue characterisation or malignancy assessment is needed
Liver function tests and CA 19-9 if carcinoma is suspected
Cross-sectional staging imaging if a mass or malignancy is identified
Assessment of surgical fitness for cholecystectomy
redFlags: Focal or asymmetric wall thickening or a soft-tissue mass suggesting carcinoma
New pain, weight loss, or jaundice
Regional lymphadenopathy or hepatic invasion on imaging
Rising tumour markers in the appropriate context
reference.prognosis: An incidentally found, uncomplicated porcelain gallbladder has a good outlook, and cholecystectomy removes both symptoms and the associated cancer risk; prognosis is poor if invasive gallbladder carcinoma has already developed, which is why the malignancy association drives management.
pitfalls: Overstating the cancer risk based on older literature, or conversely dismissing it entirely
Confusing wall calcification with a gallbladder packed with calcified stones
Overlooking a coexisting carcinoma masked by dense calcification
Delaying cholecystectomy in a fit patient when malignancy risk warrants it
Mistaking emphysematous cholecystitis for calcification on plain imaging
references: Sleisenger and Fordtran's Gastrointestinal and Liver Disease
Reviews of porcelain gallbladder and gallbladder cancer risk
Radiology literature on gallbladder wall calcification patterns
management: Cholecystectomy, generally recommended given the association with gallbladder adenocarcinoma, particularly for surgically fit patients or when calcification is selective mucosal or otherwise concerning
Laparoscopic approach for uncomplicated disease, with conversion to open resection following oncological principles if malignancy is suspected intra-operatively
Cross-sectional staging imaging and referral to hepatobiliary and oncology services when an infiltrating mass or carcinoma is identified
Assessment of surgical fitness and, in patients unfit for or declining surgery, imaging surveillance for malignant change
Discussion at a hepatobiliary multidisciplinary meeting where features are equivocal or malignancy is confirmed
